items.title: Platform Engineering Philosophy
items.text:
Three architectural principles that guide how I design and operate high-scale distributed systems:

  • Pave Golden Paths, not ticket queues

    Infrastructure complexity must be resolved in software, not human bureaucracy. Self-service APIs across AWS, OpenStack, OpenShift, and bare metal must ensure the secure, auditable, and compliant path is also the fastest and simplest for engineering teams.

  • Custom IaC philosophy & idempotent state

    Creating fresh environments is trivial; safely recovering from a failure midway through a 30-step teardown is what truly tests an engine. I design asynchronous YAML engines with DAG wave scheduling and continuous state reconciliation, eliminating the cost and vendor lock-in of commercial suites.

  • Deterministic guardrails for operational AI

    LLMs and agentic systems are untrusted components in mission-critical operations. Rather than brittle open-ended prompts, operational agents must be bounded by cyclic state machines (LangGraph), typed read-only tool contracts (MCP), and strict schema verification before emitting diagnoses or taking action.

items.title: About Me
items.text:
I'm Oscar Redondo, a Senior Platform Engineer · Python based in Madrid, Spain.

Over the last decade, my work has centered on a single question: how do you let hundreds of engineers move fast across tens of thousands of heterogeneous servers without losing governance, reliability, or sleep?

My answer is to treat internal infrastructure as a software product — paving Golden Paths through clean APIs, driver abstractions, and declarative engines where security, auditability, and recovery are built in by design rather than enforced through manual tickets.

items.title: Architectural Trajectory
items.text:
• From storage and hypervisors up: I trained in Communications Electronic Engineering at the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and began my career at Oesia operating a production OpenStack and Ceph private cloud and building a self-hosted cloud storage platform on OpenStack Swift. Starting close to storage clusters, hypervisors, and network fabrics shaped how I design higher-level abstractions today.
  • Building a bank's internal cloud platform layer by layer: Since 2017 at BBVA Technology, I have served as architect and technical lead of the central IaaS platform suite (Orion & Blueprint). Whenever an off-the-shelf tool became a scaling or licensing bottleneck, I engineered a lean Python replacement — migrating from Jenkins to a custom High-Availability Django/Celery Dispatcher, decoupling runtime configuration, executing workloads in Kubernetes Jobs, bridging F5 and OpenStack with zero downtime, and building Orion AI (PoC) with LangGraph and ReAct.
  • Open-source engineering: Outside enterprise environments, I build and maintain open-source AI and backend systems on GitHub — including OmniLecture Studio (a native Linux Wayland/GTK 3 multimodal study suite) and WrenchBuddy (a Django 6, Celery, and pgvector RAG vehicle lifecycle platform).

items.title: Engineering Principles
items.text:
• Pave Golden Paths, not ticket queues

    If an engineer needs a 20-page manual or a manual approval ticket to provision standard infrastructure, the abstraction has failed. Self-service APIs should make the compliant path the easiest path.

  • Declarative state & idempotent recovery

    Creating greenfield resources is easy; recovering from a failure halfway through a 30-step teardown is where systems are tested. Every operation should inspect live state and be safe to re-run.

  • Deterministic guardrails around AI

    LLMs and multi-agent graphs are transformative for operational triage only when treated as untrusted components — bounded by typed schemas, read-only tool contracts (MCP), and strict evidence checks.

  • End-to-end ownership & international collaboration

    Carrying the on-call pager for what you design keeps architectures honest. Sharing that architecture across teams — from mentoring junior engineers to onboarding hubs in Spain, Mexico, and Turkey — is what makes a platform last.

items.title: Engineering Notes & Architecture Essays
items.text: Reflections from a decade of building and operating internal cloud platforms: why we outgrew standard CI/CD tools, when building a lean in-house engine beats buying a commercial suite, and what actually happens when you bring agentic AI into regulated infrastructure operations.

items.title: When Shared Libraries Hit a Wall: Why We Replaced Jenkins with a Custom HA Dispatcher
items.text:
Almost every growing infrastructure organization goes through the same two-act story with Jenkins.

In Act I, teams have dozens of copy-pasted pipelines scattered across repositories. You introduce Jenkins Shared Libraries in Groovy, standardize how deployments and infrastructure tasks are triggered, cut duplication, and accelerate onboarding. It feels like a decisive engineering win — and at that stage, it is.

In Act II, your standardization succeeds so well that hundreds of engineers and automated workflows start routing thousands of daily infrastructure operations through that shared framework. That is when you discover that a CI server is not a distributed operation dispatcher.
path: When Shared Libraries Hit a Wall: Why We Replaced Jenkins with a Custom HA Dispatcher

items.title: Why Shared Libraries Were Necessary First
items.text:
Before you can replace an execution engine without breaking an organization, you need a uniform contract. Building our Jenkins Shared Libraries framework forced every team onto a common interface for triggering infrastructure tasks.

More importantly, centralizing those workflows gave us the telemetry to see where the underlying runtime was failing us at banking scale:

  1. Controller state contention: Jenkins' Groovy CPS (Continuation Passing Style) execution model serializes pipeline state back to the controller. Under heavy concurrent infrastructure workloads, the controller itself becomes a single point of contention and failure.
  2. UI-centric vs. API-first semantics: When an internal platform (like our Orion control plane) needs to trigger, poll, retry, and audit tens of thousands of daily operations programmatically, scraping build numbers and console outputs is a fragile abstraction.
  3. Configuration drift on static workers: Long-running agent VMs inevitably accumulate leftover state, credential caches, and conflicting package versions across executions.
path: When Shared Libraries Hit a Wall: Why We Replaced Jenkins with a Custom HA Dispatcher

items.title: Separating What Jenkins Bundles Together
items.text:
When we designed the migration away from Jenkins, the core architectural insight was that Jenkins bundles three concerns that should be strictly decoupled at scale:

flowchart TD
    subgraph Old["Monolithic CI Runner Model (Jenkins)"]
        J["Central Controller + Groovy CPS + Static Worker State + Inline Env Vars"]
    end

    subgraph New["Decoupled Platform Execution Architecture"]
        D["1. Scheduling & State<br/>HA Operation Dispatcher (Django + Celery + PostgreSQL/Redis)"]
        C["2. Environment Configuration<br/>Centralized Config Management (Dynamic runtime injection)"]
        K["3. Compute Isolation<br/>Kubernetes Job Execution Engine (Ephemeral containers)"]
        D --> K
        C --> K
    end

    Old -. "Architectural migration" .-> New
path: When Shared Libraries Hit a Wall: Why We Replaced Jenkins with a Custom HA Dispatcher

items.title: 1. A Purpose-Built HA Operation Dispatcher (Django + Celery)
items.text:
Instead of treating an infrastructure operation as a "build job", we modeled it as a first-class state machine in Django, PostgreSQL, Celery, and Redis, exposed via a clean Swagger/OpenAPI REST interface:

  • Callers submit a typed request and immediately receive a trackable operation identifier.
  • We gained full ownership over queue routing, exponential backoff retry logic, dead-letter handling, and step-level audit trails — running in High Availability without a single JVM controller bottleneck.
path: When Shared Libraries Hit a Wall: Why We Replaced Jenkins with a Custom HA Dispatcher

items.title: 2. Decoupling Variables from Playbook Logic
items.text:
Replacing the runner only solves half the reliability problem if teams still hardcode environment variables inside their automation repositories. Alongside the dispatcher, we built a Centralized Configuration Management System:

  • Playbooks and Ansible roles became 100% environment-agnostic.
  • At dispatch time, the configuration service resolves the target environment (dev, staging, prod) and injects the validated variable payload dynamically. Duplicated inventory branches disappeared overnight.
path: When Shared Libraries Hit a Wall: Why We Replaced Jenkins with a Custom HA Dispatcher

items.title: 3. Ephemeral Compute via Kubernetes Jobs
items.text: Finally, to eliminate worker drift, we extended the execution pipeline to run operations as isolated Kubernetes Jobs. Each operation boots a fresh, ephemeral container, receives its runtime configuration, executes the workload, streams logs and exit telemetry back to the dispatcher, and vanishes.

items.title: The Takeaway
items.text:
Standardizing on Jenkins Shared Libraries was not wasted effort — it created the abstraction boundary that later allowed us to swap out Jenkins underneath with zero disruption to the engineering teams consuming it.

items.title: Nine Years of Internal Cloud Platforms: Why Declarative YAML Replaced Our Commercial Orchestrator
items.text:
"Never build your own orchestrator" is generally good advice — until you look closely at what your organization already owns and where commercial suites actually spend your engineering budget.

When we evaluated how 500+ engineers should orchestrate full infrastructure environments across our hybrid cloud, the default enterprise option on the table was a commercial suite like Red Hat Automation Platform (Ansible Tower). Instead, we built Blueprint: an asynchronous, declarative Python lifecycle engine driven by versioned YAML blueprints.

Here is why that trade-off made sense for us, what we chose not to build, and why teardown — not creation — is the true test of any infrastructure engine.
path: Nine Years of Internal Cloud Platforms: Why Declarative YAML Replaced Our Commercial Orchestrator

items.title: 1. Owning the Control Plane Changes the Build-vs-Buy Calculus
items.text:
Most teams adopt heavy external orchestrators because they have no unified API over their underlying infrastructure.

We were in a different position. Over several years, we had already built Orion, our central IaaS platform governing tens of thousands of nodes across AWS, OpenStack, OpenShift, and bare-metal behind a single driver-based REST API. Orion already handled:

  • Authentication, RBAC, and compliance policies.
  • Provider-specific driver translation.
  • Live multi-cloud inventory across PostgreSQL and MongoDB.
  • Job tracking and immutable audit trails.

Buying a commercial orchestration suite to sit in front of Orion meant paying per-node licensing fees across tens of thousands of machines just to sequence HTTP calls against an API we already owned — while losing native visibility into Orion's job identifiers when a multi-step deployment failed halfway through.
path: Nine Years of Internal Cloud Platforms: Why Declarative YAML Replaced Our Commercial Orchestrator

items.title: 2. Why We Avoided Local State Files
items.text:
Tools inspired by Terraform often copy its most operationally painful design choice: a separate state file (tfstate) that must be stored, locked, and reconciled against reality whenever someone makes an out-of-band change.

Because Blueprint was designed specifically for Orion, we made a deliberate architectural decision: no separate state files.

flowchart LR
    Manifest["Versioned YAML Blueprint<br/>(Desired State in Git)"] --> Engine["Blueprint Async Engine<br/>(DAG & Delta Resolver)"]
    Orion[("Orion Control Plane<br/>(Live Observed State)")] --> Engine
    Engine -->|"Execute only the delta<br/>(Concurrent waves)"| Orion
    Engine --> Report["Structured Audit Report<br/>(Mapped to Orion Job IDs)"]

Orion's hybrid database is the live source of truth. Before Blueprint executes a wave of operations, it queries Orion directly for the current state of the declared resources and acts only on the delta. There is no state file to corrupt, no stale lock after a crashed CI runner, and no drift between "orchestrator state" and "platform inventory".
path: Nine Years of Internal Cloud Platforms: Why Declarative YAML Replaced Our Commercial Orchestrator

items.title: 3. Creation Is Easy; Idempotent Teardown Is the Real Test
items.text:
Almost any script can provision a greenfield environment when every API returns 200 OK. Where procedural automation falls apart is partial failure during teardown.

Imagine tearing down a 25-resource environment (compute pools, load balancer rules, storage volumes, networks). Step 14 times out because an upstream cloud API is momentarily degraded. What happens when the engineer re-runs the destroy job five minutes later?

  • In procedural playbooks: Step 1 tries to delete a resource that was already deleted in the first run, fails with 404 Not Found, and aborts the entire pipeline — forcing an engineer to manually comment out steps or clean up resources by hand.
  • In Blueprint: Every step in a reverse-dependency teardown queries Orion first. Steps 1 through 13 see that their target resources are already gone, record a clean no-op, and the engine resumes immediately at Step 14.

Making teardown safe to repeat turned environment decommissioning from a high-stress manual ticket into a routine self-service operation.
path: Nine Years of Internal Cloud Platforms: Why Declarative YAML Replaced Our Commercial Orchestrator

items.title: 4. The Honest Cost of Building In-House
items.text:
Owning your orchestration engine eliminates commercial licensing and gives you a tight fit with internal compliance, but it is not free:

  • You own the edge cases: Cycle detection in dependency graphs, partial failure reporting, and schema evolution are now your team's responsibility.
  • Documentation is a first-class engineering deliverable: A commercial tool comes with public Stack Overflow answers; an internal YAML DSL only succeeds if its error messages, schema validation, and golden-path templates are self-explanatory.

After nine years of evolving this stack, the lesson is straightforward: don't reinvent commodity cloud SDKs — encapsulate them behind drivers. But when the orchestration layer sits directly between your engineers, your auditors, and your core control plane, a lean, well-bounded Python engine can outperform a heavyweight commercial suite in both reliability and cost.

items.title: The PoC Was the Easy Part: Lessons from Building an Agentic CI/CD Diagnostic Engine in Banking
items.text:
Most engineering posts about AI agents end at the moment the prototype works on a benchmark dataset. In a regulated enterprise, that is actually where the hardest part begins.

When we designed and validated the Orion AI Proof of Concept (PoC) at BBVA — a multi-agent system built with LangGraph and ReAct loops to automate CI/CD root-cause failure analysis — the technical goal was clear: stop engineers from spending hours digging through endless execution logs, internal runbooks, and GitLab commit diffs every time a pipeline failed.

The prototype worked: it slashed triage from hours of manual log correlation to seconds. Yet its current status — validated and prepared, awaiting integration guidelines for central AI infrastructure — taught me just as much about enterprise platform architecture as writing the LangGraph nodes themselves.
path: The PoC Was the Easy Part: Lessons from Building an Agentic CI/CD Diagnostic Engine in Banking

items.title: 1. Why Linear LLM Chains Fail at Incident Triage
items.text:
Early experiments with LLM-assisted ops usually follow a naive linear recipe: take the tail of a failed build log, paste it into a prompt, and ask the model what went wrong.

In real infrastructure pipelines, that fails for two reasons:

  1. The root cause is rarely in the last 50 lines: A build failure at minute 18 is often caused by an environment variable or network timeout that happened at minute 2.
  2. Logs tell you what broke, not what changed: An exit code in a deployment log is ambiguous until you correlate it with the recent GitLab commit diff or a known operational runbook.

That is why we modeled Orion AI as a stateful, cyclic graph in LangGraph rather than a linear chain:

flowchart TD
    Event["Pipeline Failure Event"] --> Supervisor["LangGraph Supervisor"]
    Supervisor --> Logs["Execution Logs"]
    Supervisor --> Docs["Support Runbooks (Redis RAG Cache)"]
    Supervisor --> Diffs["GitLab Commit Diffs"]
    Logs & Docs & Diffs --> ReAct["ReAct Reasoning (Qwen 131k Context)"]
    ReAct --> Gate{"Deterministic Guardrails"}
    Gate -- "Insufficient evidence → inspect deeper diff" --> Diffs
    Gate -- "Grounded & schema-valid" --> Diagnosis["Actionable Root-Cause Report"]
  • Concurrent context gathering: The graph pulls raw execution traces, operational runbooks (cached in Redis to accelerate RAG retrieval), and repository metadata in parallel.
  • Long-context correlation (Qwen 131k): Feeding consolidated evidence into a high-context model preserves the causal chain from initialization to failure.
  • Bounded ReAct loops: When a log trace points to a modified configuration file, the agent loops back to inspect the exact commit diff before formulating its diagnosis.
path: The PoC Was the Easy Part: Lessons from Building an Agentic CI/CD Diagnostic Engine in Banking

items.title: 2. Deterministic Guardrails: Treating the LLM as an Untrusted Component
items.text:
In banking operations, a hallucinated remediation command is worse than no diagnosis at all. To make the PoC trustworthy for engineers, we applied standard distributed-systems discipline to the model's inputs and outputs:

  • Strict output schemas: The agent cannot return free-form prose; it must populate a typed diagnostic contract.
  • Explicit evidence grounding: Every root-cause claim must point to concrete evidence retrieved during the run (log fragments, runbook entries, or commit diffs).
  • Isolated tool contracts (MCP): External systems (Orion Dispatcher, Redis runbook cache, GitLab) are queried through strictly typed read-only tool interfaces rather than giving the agent arbitrary shell access.
path: The PoC Was the Easy Part: Lessons from Building an Agentic CI/CD Diagnostic Engine in Banking

items.title: 3. Why a Validated PoC Still Waits on Enterprise Foundations
items.text:
Once the PoC was validated against real failure scenarios, why didn't we immediately wire it into every production pipeline the next morning?

Because in a large financial institution, an operational AI agent sits at the intersection of two separate platform domains: Infrastructure Operations (which we own) and Central Corporate AI Infrastructure (owned by partner platform teams).

Moving from a validated prototype to organization-wide production requires three cross-team foundations to be in place:

  1. Shared inference capacity & routing standards: Productionizing high-context (131k token) agent runs across hundreds of daily pipeline failures requires formal capacity allocation and integration standards on the bank's centralized LLM inference clusters.
  2. Operational data governance: CI/CD logs and commit diffs inevitably touch internal hostnames, configuration metadata, and repository structures. Formalizing how operational telemetry is redacted, transmitted, and retained by shared internal AI endpoints is a mandatory governance milestone.
  3. Clear ownership of the evaluation loop: In production, models and prompts drift as infrastructure evolves. Defining who owns the continuous evaluation dataset and SLOs for diagnostic accuracy is just as important as the code.
path: The PoC Was the Easy Part: Lessons from Building an Agentic CI/CD Diagnostic Engine in Banking

items.title: The Takeaway for Platform Engineers
items.text:
If you are building agentic systems for real-world operations, design your state graph, tool boundaries, and deterministic guardrails so the system is ready for production from day one — and keep your architecture decoupled from any single model endpoint so that when central AI infrastructure guidelines land, integration is a configuration change rather than a rewrite.

items.title: Blueprint: Asynchronous Declarative Lifecycle Engine
items.text:
Dimension Details Role Architect & Platform Lead Organization BBVA (Core Banking Infrastructure) Outcome Eliminated commercial orchestration licensing (Red Hat Automation Platform); brought declarative GitOps and resumable teardowns to Orion Stack Python, AsyncIO, Declarative YAML DSL, JSON Schema, GitOps, Orion REST API

Architectural summary

Blueprint is an internal asynchronous orchestration engine in Python — conceptually analogous to Terraform, purpose-built for BBVA's Orion platform. Engineering teams declare the desired state of complete environments in versioned YAML blueprints; the engine resolves the dependency graph into concurrent waves, reconciles against live Orion state, produces immutable audit traces per Job ID, and supports idempotent destroy workflows that safely resume interrupted teardowns without rework.

items.title: 1. Context & Why Commercial Suites Did Not Fit
items.text:
Once Orion unified the APIs of AWS, OpenStack, OpenShift, and bare metal, engineering teams needed to orchestrate multi-tier environments (networks, load balancers, compute pools, middleware) as a single declarative unit.

Relying on commercial orchestration suites such as Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform / Tower presented three prohibitive roadblocks:

  1. Per-node licensing & third-party concentration risk (DORA): Commercial node-based licensing penalized fleet growth and increased critical vendor lock-in contrary to financial resilience mandates.
  2. Mid-run failure opacity: When a 40-step procedural workflow failed at step 27, reconstructing exact state or safely tearing down the partial environment required manual intervention.
  3. Impedance mismatch with Orion: Orion was already the established source of truth. We needed an engine that natively understood its Job IDs, async polling contracts, RBAC model, and compliance reports.

items.title: 2. Abstract System Topology: Orchestration Lifecycle
items.text:
Blueprint processes declarative manifests through a strict asynchronous pipeline:

flowchart LR
    Plan["1. Declarative Plan<br/><b>(YAML Manifest in Git)</b>"] --> DAG["2. Blueprint Engine<br/><b>(Validation & DAG Waves)</b>"]
    DAG --> Orion["3. Orion IaaS API<br/><b>(AsyncIO Execution)</b>"]
    Orion --> Teardown["4. Lifecycle<br/><b>(Idempotent Teardowns)</b>"]
    Teardown --> Audit[("5. Audit Trace<br/><b>(Job ID Ledger)</b>")]

items.title: Step-by-Step Execution Pipeline
items.text: Stage Responsible Component Exactly What Executes Engineering Guarantee 1. Pre-Flight Validation JSON Schema Validator (Python) Strict type checking, syntax constraints, and circular dependency detection in YAML before touching production. Immediate rejection of invalid manifests without firing downstream API calls. 2. DAG Scheduling Dependency Scheduler Construction of the directed acyclic graph and task partitioning into concurrent execution waves. Automatically inverts dependency order for teardowns. Maximum parallelism strictly respecting network and service topology. 3. Live State Inspection Orion REST Connector Queries real resource state against Orion's live inventory to calculate the execution delta. Clean omission of already satisfied steps (NO-OP), eliminating redundant operations. 4. Asynchronous Execution AsyncIO Engine Dispatches concurrent API calls against Orion for all resources within the active wave, tracking each returned Job ID. High concurrency without thread blocking and with minimal memory footprint. 5. Audit Report Forensic Trace Generator Emits a structured audit trace linking every declared resource to its exact Orion Job IDs, timestamps, and state transitions. Immutable, 100% auditable evidence for regulatory banking compliance.

items.title: A. Concurrent DAG Waves via Python AsyncIO
items.text: Infrastructure provisioning is fundamentally I/O-bound (waiting on cloud APIs, hypervisors, and network appliances). Blueprint partitions the dependency graph into execution waves: independent resources run concurrently over Python's AsyncIO event loop, while downstream resources await upstream wave completion. This cut overall deployment times by over 60% compared to sequential procedural execution.

items.title: B. Idempotent Teardowns & Orphan-Free Resumption
items.text: The most fragile point of traditional automation is environment decommissioning. If a teardown fails midway, naive scripts crash upon re-execution because the initial resources are already gone. Blueprint inverts the DAG and queries live state in Orion before acting: destroyed resources evaluate as NO-OP, allowing teardowns to resume cleanly without manual database fixes.

items.title: C. Job ID Audit Trails vs. Local State Files (tfstate)
items.text: Rather than relying on local or remote state files susceptible to corruption and split-brain concurrency locks, Blueprint treats Orion as the live source of truth. Every operation is tied to an immutable Orion Job ID, producing verifiable forensic audit trails consumed directly by regulatory inspectors.

items.title: 4. Failure Modes & Resilience Design
items.text: Failure Scenario Traditional Procedural Approach Blueprint Engine Behavior Circular dependency in manifest Discovered mid-deployment after mutating production Rejected during pre-flight DAG resolution before any API call Timeout halfway through a 20-node teardown Re-run crashes on "resource not found" for nodes 1–10 Re-run inspects Orion state, skips nodes 1–10, and resumes at node 11 Auditor requests proof of a failed change Manual correlation across scattered console logs Structured report maps every step to its immutable Orion Job ID

items.title: 5. Architectural Trade-Offs
items.text: Decision Alternative Considered Trade-Off Rationale Purpose-built Python engine Red Hat Automation Platform / Terraform Eliminated recurring commercial licensing, mitigated third-party concentration risk (DORA), and integrated natively with Orion's job/audit model. Orion as live source of truth Local state files (tfstate equivalent) Orion already tracks live multi-cloud inventory; querying Orion directly prevents state-file drift and split-brain locks. AsyncIO concurrency Multi-threaded / multi-process runners High concurrency for hundreds of simultaneous API waits with minimal memory footprint.

items.title: 6. Operational & Business Impact
items.text:
• Commercial license elimination: Architecting an in-house declarative engine natively integrated with Orion eliminated reliance on commercial node-licensed suites (such as Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform / Tower), contributing directly to the €6M+ cumulative cost avoidance across the platform.
  • Idempotent & resumable teardowns: 100% success rate on interrupted or re-executed environment destructions without leaving orphaned resources or requiring manual database interventions.
  • High-throughput asynchronous concurrency: Reduced multi-tier environment provisioning time by over 60% through DAG wave concurrency executed on Python's AsyncIO event loop.
  • Job ID audit trail (DORA Alignment): Automatically generated, immutable audit evidence tying every Git-versioned manifest to Orion's internal execution Job IDs for regulatory banking compliance and change risk governance.

items.title: Leaving Jenkins at Scale: HA Operation Dispatcher, Runtime Configuration & K8s Execution
items.text:
Dimension Details Role Architect & Platform Lead Organization BBVA (Core Banking Infrastructure) Scope Replaced Jenkins as the infrastructure execution backbone; unified configuration management and ephemeral Kubernetes execution Stack Python, Django, DRF, Celery, Redis, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes Jobs, Ansible, Groovy

Architectural summary

Before an internal platform can scale to tens of thousands of daily operations, its underlying execution engine must be reliable, API-driven, and stateless. This case study covers an architectural evolution: standardizing pipelines with Jenkins Shared Libraries, overcoming the monolith's bottlenecks by migrating to an in-house HA Dispatcher (Django + Celery), decoupling variables via a Centralized Configuration Service, and isolating execution in Kubernetes Jobs.

items.title: 1. The Operational Bottlenecks of Jenkins
items.text:
We initially standardized enterprise automation using a modular Jenkins Shared Libraries framework in Groovy. While it slashed duplication across teams, operating at banking scale revealed structural ceilings within Jenkins:

  1. Master controller fragility (SPOF): Massive concurrent infrastructure executions strained the JVM master process and Groovy CPS serialization, threatening platform availability and compromising business continuity mandates under DORA.
  2. Deficient programmatic control: Managing thousands of daily infrastructure workflows via Jenkins' web-centric APIs lacked a relational state model and granular back-pressure controls.
  3. Static agent drift: Long-lived worker nodes accumulated residual state, dependency clashes, and noisy-neighbor resource contention.

items.title: 2. Abstract System Topology: Decoupling Execution from State
items.text:
The architecture decouples the execution lifecycle into five distinct stages:

flowchart LR
    Callers["Callers<br/><b>(Orion · Blueprint · CI/CD)</b>"] --> Disp["1. HA Dispatcher<br/><b>(Django + Celery)</b>"]
    Disp --> Config["2. Config Service<br/><b>(Runtime Injection)</b>"]
    Config --> K8s["3. K8s Jobs<br/><b>(Ephemeral Pods)</b>"]
    K8s --> Playbook["4. Ansible Core<br/><b>(Agnostic Roles)</b>"]
    Playbook --> State[("5. Telemetry<br/><b>(PostgreSQL + Redis)</b>")]

items.title: Step-by-Step Execution Pipeline
items.text: Stage Responsible Component Exactly What Executes Engineering Guarantee 1. Async Dispatch OpenAPI REST Gateway & Celery Workers Reception of the operation trigger from Orion, Blueprint, or CI/CD; initial state persistence in PostgreSQL. High-availability, non-blocking ingestion (zero SPOF). 2. Config Injection Centralized Configuration Service Detects target environment (Dev/Staging/Prod) and dynamically injects secrets and parameters into memory at runtime. Total eradication of configuration drift across environments. 3. Ephemeral Launch Kubernetes Job Controller Spawns a dedicated, short-lived container pod with the exact image and dependencies required for the job. Strict compute isolation and guaranteed clean dependencies. 4. Agnostic Execution Containerized Ansible Runner Executes 100% environment-agnostic roles (GitLab, Artifactory, core banking services) against target nodes. Exact same tested automation code runs across dev, staging, and production. 5. Streaming & Teardown Redis Broker & PostgreSQL State Store Continuously streams execution logs, captures exit codes, seals final state, and destroys the pod. Zero residual state on workers and complete audit history.

items.title: A. Custom Django/Celery Dispatcher vs. Scaling Jenkins Controllers
items.text: Scaling out Jenkins controllers multiplied plugin maintenance overhead and did not solve state coupling. Building a lightweight Python dispatcher with Celery and PostgreSQL provided native REST API control, prioritized queues, and a durable relational state machine, allowing seamless workload migration from Shared Libraries without downtime.

items.title: B. Dynamic Runtime Configuration Injection vs. Duplicated Repositories
items.text: To eradicate the practice of duplicating playbooks across dev, staging, and prod branches, we built a service that decouples configuration from automation: Ansible roles are 100% environment-agnostic, and variables are resolved and injected into memory at runtime, guaranteeing the exact same tested artifact reaches production.

items.title: C. Ephemeral Kubernetes Jobs vs. Long-Lived Static Workers
items.text: Traditional shared worker VMs accumulated leftover files and colliding dependencies. Migrating execution to Kubernetes Jobs turned every task into an ephemeral pod that provisions on demand, executes in isolation, and terminates immediately after emitting telemetry, completely removing worker host maintenance.

items.title: 4. Architectural Trade-Offs
items.text: Decision Alternative Considered Trade-Off Rationale In-house Django/Celery HA Dispatcher Scale out multi-controller Jenkins Eliminated the JVM master SPOF, fulfilling operational resilience and business continuity requirements under DORA with native REST API control. Runtime variable injection Per-environment Git branches / inventories Removed duplicated configuration sets across repositories and guaranteed the exact same tested role runs in dev, staging, and production. Ephemeral Kubernetes Jobs Static worker VMs Eliminated environment drift, dependency clashes, and noisy-neighbor contention across concurrent runs.

items.title: 5. Operational & Business Impact
items.text:
• Zero SPOF & DORA Operational Resilience (100% HA): Eliminated the fragility of Jenkins' monolithic master controller for infrastructure workflows, eradicating single points of failure (SPOF) and ensuring business continuity mandated by financial digital resilience frameworks during host outages.
  • Zero Configuration Drift: Dynamic runtime variable injection from a centralized service into environment-agnostic Ansible roles completely eradicated configuration divergences across dev, staging, and production.
  • Compute Isolation & Efficiency: Replaced static long-lived worker agents with ephemeral Kubernetes Jobs, running tasks in isolated containers that release resources immediately upon completion with zero residual state.
  • Proven Banking Scale: Governed and dispatched 40,000+ daily operations with real-time state tracking in PostgreSQL and Redis.

items.title: OmniLecture Studio: Native Linux Multimodal AI Suite
items.text:
Dimension Details Role Creator & Maintainer (Open Source) Repository github.com/oredondo/omnilecture-studio (MIT License) Domain Linux desktop engineering (Wayland / GNOME / GTK 3) & multimodal LangGraph pipelines Stack Python 3.10+, GTK 3, D-Bus Screencast, GStreamer, FFmpeg, LangGraph, faster-whisper (int8), Whisper API, OpenCV (CLAHE), Tesseract OCR

Architectural summary

OmniLecture Studio is an open-source academic and technical productivity suite built natively for Linux desktops (GNOME / Wayland and X11). It combines native screen and audio capture via system APIs, an advanced FFmpeg acoustic conditioning pipeline for voice dictations, speech filtering in Whisper to prevent hallucinations, and a multi-node LangGraph engine that synthesizes content into interconnected Markdown (.md) knowledge graphs (compatible with Obsidian and PKM tools) alongside spaced-repetition Anki flashcard decks under strict zero-invention guardrails.

items.title: 1. Context & Engineering Challenges
items.text:
Automating the processing of technical lectures, conferences, and voice dictations on Linux presented three critical engineering challenges:

  1. Acoustic noise & transcription hallucinations: Raw audio (breathing, keyboard clicks, dead silence, background hum) frequently drives Whisper into infinite repetition loops or hallucinated phrases.
  2. Compute & storage overhead: Standard screen recording tools capture video at 30/60 FPS, creating massive, inefficient files for content where the majority of the display (slides, terminals, code) remains static.
  3. Loss of conceptual relationships: Dumping notes into flat, linear text blocks discards the semantic richness of a technical session, hindering the connection between interdependent concepts.

items.title: 2. Abstract System Topology: Multimodal & Dictation Pipeline
items.text:
OmniLecture Studio decouples capture, signal preprocessing, filtered transcription, and conceptual synthesis into a deterministic pipeline:

flowchart LR
    In["1. Native Ingestion<br/><b>(Audio · Screen · Handwritten)</b>"] --> FFmpeg["2. FFmpeg Preprocessing<br/><b>(Bandpass · afftdn · Silenceremove)</b>"]
    FFmpeg --> Whisper["3. Filtered Whisper<br/><b>(VAD · Temp Fallback · Anti-Loop)</b>"]
    Whisper --> Graph["4. LangGraph Engine<br/><b>(30-min Windows · Zero Invention)</b>"]
    Graph --> MD[("5. Markdown Graphs<br/><b>(Obsidian · Wikilinks · Anki)</b>")]

items.title: Step-by-Step Processing Pipeline
items.text: Stage Responsible Component Exactly What Executes Engineering Guarantee 1. Native Ingestion GTK 3, D-Bus Screencast & GStreamer Desktop video screencast via GNOME Portal; system and microphone audio mixing via PipeWire/PulseAudio. Native, secure capture without root privileges or browser-wrapper overhead. 2. FFmpeg Conditioning Multimedia Pipeline (processor.py) FFT spectral denoising (afftdn), speech bandpass (100 Hz–4000 Hz), dead silence removal (silenceremove), and 10 FPS H.264 encoding (-tune stillimage). Up to 70% video size reduction and pristine, normalized audio tuned for inference. 3. Filtered Whisper Dual Transcription Engine Voice Activity Detection (VAD), compression ratio thresholding, temperature fallback, and dual-engine execution (faster-whisper int8 local or cloud API in 10-min chunks). Zero infinite loops: elimination of hallucinations during pauses and low resource consumption (< 1 GB RAM on CPU). 4. LangGraph Orchestration Stateful Cyclic Graph Session partitioning into 30-minute processing windows, multimodal slide OCR correlation (CLAHE + Tesseract), and reflective evaluation. Temporal coherence and full traceability without context dilution during long sessions. 5. Markdown Graph Synthesis Conceptual Network Generator Structured Markdown (.md) generation with bidirectional wikilinks ([[concept]]), YAML frontmatter metadata, and Anki card decks. Native integration with Obsidian and PKM tools for semantic graph exploration.

items.title: A. FFmpeg Acoustic Conditioning for Dictation & Speech
items.text: Audio preprocessing in FFmpeg serves as the primary line of defense to guarantee accurate technical dictation transcripts: - FFT spectral denoising (afftdn): Eliminates continuous background hum (system cooling fans, electrical noise) before the waveform reaches the speech model. - Strict vocal bandpass (100 Hz–4000 Hz): Filters out low-frequency mechanical rumble (desk vibrations) and high-frequency harmonics outside human speech formants. - Intelligent silence stripping (silenceremove): Trims extended pauses and dead air that commonly trigger hallucinations in phonetic inference engines. - Tuned visual compression: 10 FPS H.264 encoding with -tune stillimage and CRF 24 preserves razor-sharp edges on typography and code while slashing storage footprint by up to 70%.

items.title: B. Advanced Filters & Anti-Hallucination Controls in Whisper
items.text: To counter Whisper's tendency to loop or hallucinate text when audio signal degrades, the pipeline enforces strict phonetic guardrails: - Voice Activity Detection (VAD): Discards silent or low-energy segments prior to invoking the neural network. - Temperature Fallback: Begins inference at temperature 0.0 (maximum determinism) and only steps up temperature if the compression ratio exceeds compression_ratio_threshold (2.4), preventing phrase repetition cascades. - Dual execution engine: Allows seamless toggling between an offline faster-whisper engine quantized in int8 (running on CPU with under 1 GB RAM without sending data over the network) and the remote Whisper API with automatic 10-minute chunking.

items.title: C. Markdown (.md) Knowledge Graphs & LangGraph Orchestration
items.text: OmniLecture avoids closed, proprietary document formats in favor of interconnected Markdown knowledge graphs: - Stateful LangGraph machine: Orchestrates the session across consecutive 30-minute windows (Segmentation → Entity Extraction → Refinement), preventing context degradation on multi-hour recordings. - Semantic interlinking (Obsidian Knowledge Graphs): Every key concept, formula, or definition is linked via bidirectional wikilinks ([[Key Concept]]) and hierarchical taxonomies in Markdown (.md), enabling full semantic graph visualization in Obsidian and Personal Knowledge Management (PKM) ecosystems. - Spaced repetition: Automatically outputs Anki flashcard decks mapped to concepts within the graph, ensuring long-term knowledge retention.

items.title: 4. Architectural Trade-Offs
items.text: Decision Alternative Considered Trade-Off Rationale Upstream FFmpeg conditioning Feeding raw audio directly to Whisper Eliminates background hum and silence that provoke infinite repetition loops and hallucinations. VAD & Temperature Fallback filters Standard single-pass fixed-temperature inference Prevents repetitive phrase generation and enforces deterministic transcription outputs. Markdown knowledge graphs (.md) Proprietary word-processing formats Models linked conceptual networks via wikilinks compatible with Obsidian and versionable in Git. Dual Whisper (int8 local + Cloud) Cloud-only or heavy unquantized local model Delivers full privacy and low compute (< 1 GB CPU RAM) offline, while retaining cloud capacity for massive recordings. 30-minute LangGraph windows Single monolithic prompt over entire transcript Prevents context window saturation and preserves granular technical detail across multi-hour lectures.

items.text:

items.title: Orion AI: Operational AI & Auto-Diagnostic Engine for CI/CD (Validated PoC)
items.text:
Dimension Details Role Architect & Technical Lead Organization / Stage BBVA · Validated Proof of Concept (PoC) Outcome Validated prototype reducing incident log triage from hours to seconds; prepared and awaiting central AI infrastructure integration guidelines Stack Python, LangGraph, ReAct Agents, Qwen LLM (131k context), Model Context Protocol (MCP), Redis, Dispatcher & GitLab APIs

Architectural summary

Orion AI is a functional, validated Proof of Concept (PoC) built to evaluate parallel, multi-agent root-cause diagnostics across CI/CD and infrastructure pipelines. Using LangGraph state machines and ReAct reasoning loops, the system concurrently aggregates execution logs, operational runbooks in Redis cache, and GitLab commit diffs with high-context LLMs (Qwen 131k context) under strict deterministic guardrails — cutting manual triage from hours to seconds during validation.

items.title: 1. Operational Problem Statement
items.text:
When enterprise CI/CD pipelines or infrastructure deployments fail, Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) is overwhelmingly dominated by manual context gathering. In a banking environment subject to frameworks like DORA, rapid ICT incident detection and triage is a critical regulatory priority: 1. Sifting through extensive Orion execution logs in the Dispatcher to isolate the first genuine error trace. 2. Searching internal wikis and historical incident tickets for known failure patterns. 3. Inspecting recent GitLab repository diffs to correlate code or configuration changes.

Goal of the PoC: Prove that an autonomous multi-agent workflow can synthesize those three evidence sources concurrently and emit an accurate, zero-hallucination root-cause diagnosis within seconds.

items.title: 2. Abstract System Topology: Multi-Agent Diagnostic Pipeline
items.text:
Orion AI structures root-cause analysis as a sequential workflow with reflective loops:

flowchart LR
    Fail["Execution Failure<br/><b>(Orion Log in Dispatcher)</b>"] --> Sup["1. LangGraph<br/><b>(Stateful Supervisor)</b>"]
    Sup --> Evid["2. Evidence<br/><b>(Logs · Redis · GitLab)</b>"]
    Evid --> ReAct["3. ReAct Loop<br/><b>(Qwen 131k + MCP)</b>"]
    ReAct --> Guard["4. Guardrails<br/><b>(Strict Pydantic)</b>"]
    Guard --> Report[("5. Diagnosis<br/><b>(Grounded Root Cause)</b>")]

items.title: Step-by-Step Diagnostic Pipeline
items.text: Stage Responsible Component Exactly What Executes Engineering Guarantee 1. Failure Ingestion Webhook / API Listener Ingests the failure event and Orion log from the Dispatcher with the Job ID and initial exit code. Instant diagnostic trigger without manual developer intervention. 2. Concurrent Gathering LangGraph Parallel Nodes Fetches full execution logs, operational runbooks from Redis cache, and recent GitLab commit diffs in parallel. Millisecond context aggregation without serial I/O bottlenecks. 3. Multimodal Reasoning ReAct Loop (Qwen 131k) Evaluates consolidated evidence across the 131k token window to isolate the failure's root cause. Detects broken dependencies, environment drift, or subtle Git changes. 4. Deterministic Check Pydantic Schema Guardrails Verifies that every assertion in the diagnostic output maps directly to actual logs, runbooks, or diffs. Zero hallucination: outright rejection of ungrounded hypotheses. 5. Diagnostic Emission Incident Report Generator Emits a structured summary containing the exact failure line, culprit commit, and recommended remediation action. Drops MTTR from hours to seconds for on-call operations teams.

items.title: A. Cyclic Stateful Graphs (LangGraph) vs. Linear Chains
items.text: Pipeline failures are rarely diagnosable in a single linear pass. When a raw log only shows a generic exit code, the agent needs to loop back and inspect recent commit diffs before concluding. LangGraph maintains a typed state across nodes, enabling conditional branching and bounded ReAct loops impossible in traditional linear chains.

items.title: B. High-Context Reasoning Window (131k) vs. Chunked Fragmentation
items.text: Rather than fragmenting build logs through standard vector RAG chunking that loses causality between distant execution phases, the system streams consolidated context into a 131k-token model (Qwen), preserving the full operational timeline from initialization to the terminal crash.

items.title: C. Strict Deterministic Guardrails vs. Free-Form Text
items.text: In a regulated banking environment, an operational diagnostic agent cannot speculate. Responses are strictly validated against typed Pydantic contracts and tool integrations (logs, GitLab) are isolated behind Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces, eradicating hallucinations and ensuring every finding maps directly to grounded evidence.

items.title: 4. Architectural Trade-Offs
items.text: Decision Alternative Considered Trade-Off Rationale Stateful cyclic graphs (LangGraph) Linear chains or single-turn prompts Enabled reflective conditional retries and backtracking to code diff inspection when logs are ambiguous. Self-hosted long-context LLM (Qwen 131k) Public cloud black-box APIs Protected sensitive banking source code while accommodating entire execution histories in a single context window. Strict typed deterministic guardrails (Pydantic) Unstructured free-form text output Completely eliminated hallucinated diagnostic commands, ensuring all outputs map directly to grounded evidence.

items.title: 5. Why This Is a Validated PoC — and Enterprise Rollout Constraints
items.text:
[!IMPORTANT] Including the real organizational constraints behind a PoC is essential to an honest architectural post-mortem.

The technical prototype was fully built, tested against real failure scenarios, and validated. However, moving an LLM-powered system to wide production rollout inside a tier-1 bank depends on cross-cutting corporate factors:

  1. Central AI inference infrastructure: Requires standardized guidelines and capacity allocation on shared internal GPU platforms managed by dedicated corporate AI teams.
  2. Operational data privacy & governance: Routing CI/CD logs and source code into inference endpoints requires formal cross-team definitions around retention, redaction, and multi-tenant isolation.
  3. Key engineering takeaway: Building a reliable LangGraph + ReAct agent with deterministic guardrails is the tractable engineering problem; aligning shared corporate GPU platforms and governance boundaries is what sets adoption timelines in regulated industries.

items.title: 6. Operational Impact & Validation
items.text:
• Radical MTTR reduction (DORA Alignment): Reduced root cause isolation time for complex CI/CD pipeline failures from hours of manual digging to under 15 seconds, supporting rapid ICT incident response thresholds mandated by DORA.
  • Zero-hallucination multi-source correlation: Proved the capability to synthesize runtime logs, Redis-cached runbooks, and GitLab diffs concurrently under strict evidence schemas.
  • Agentic architecture blueprint: Established reference patterns for graph-based multi-agent orchestration, MCP contracts, and deterministic guardrails for operational AI across the bank.

items.title: Orion: Central IaaS Platform & Universal Driver Pipeline
items.text:
Dimension Details Role Architect & Platform Lead Organization BBVA (Core Banking Infrastructure) Scale 30,000+ governed machines · 40,000+ daily operations · 500+ engineers Stack Python, Django, DRF, Celery, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Ansible, AWS, OpenStack, OpenShift, Infoblox

Architectural summary

Orion is the central control plane for infrastructure governance, comprehensive auditing, and self-service deployment across BBVA's hybrid cloud. It abstracts four technological substrates (AWS, OpenStack, OpenShift, and physical bare-metal) behind an OpenAPI-documented REST interface, web self-service forms, and automation schedulers, combining a universal driver provisioning pipeline, two-layer Ansible configuration (corporate Ground + User workloads), and an end-to-end machine traceability audit engine.

items.title: 1. The Evolution of Orion: From CMDB to a High-Availability Dispatcher
items.text:
Orion was not built as a static monolithic tool, but as an evolving architectural response to enterprise scaling bottlenecks within BBVA:

  • Phase 1 · Origin (CMDB & API-First Inventory): A centralized control plane to govern heterogeneous multi-cloud assets via hybrid persistence (PostgreSQL + MongoDB + Redis) and a REST catalog with RBAC permissions.
  • Phase 2 · The Jenkins Bottleneck: Execution initially relied on a centralized Jenkins cluster that lacked native high availability (critical SPOF), had a rigid UI for operational workflows, and introduced high maintenance overhead.
  • Phase 3 · Emergence of the Integrated HA Dispatcher: Orion absorbed the execution plane by developing an in-house HA Dispatcher (Django + Celery + Kubernetes Jobs), decoupling runtime variables and structuring provisioning into cloud drivers and layered Ansible pipelines.
  • Phase 4 · Declarative Extension & AI (Blueprint & Orion AI): Unification with declarative orchestration via Blueprint (YAML engine with DAGs) and agentic CI/CD failure diagnostics with Orion AI (LangGraph).

items.title: 2. Context & Problem Statement
items.text:
Operating tens of thousands of banking workloads across public cloud, private cloud, and on-premises data centers created three critical challenges:

  1. Siloed provisioning: Target environments required isolated tools and credentials, turning simple requests into multi-day manual handoffs.
  2. Audit blindness & dispersed tracking: Strict regulatory banking mandates (such as DORA resilience frameworks and ECB/EBA guidelines) require knowing at any moment who authorized an asset, exactly what software packages are installed, and its full historical event log.
  3. Configuration drift & baseline vulnerabilities: Without an enforced separation between the bank's operational baseline (security, monitoring) and user applications, systems drifted from corporate compliance.

items.title: 3. Abstract System Topology: Operation Lifecycle
items.text:
Orion centralizes the banking infrastructure lifecycle through a strict sequential pipeline:

flowchart LR
    Trig["Trigger<br/><b>(Web UI · API · Scheduler)</b>"] --> Disp["HA Dispatcher<br/><b>(RBAC & Celery)</b>"]
    Disp --> Prov["1. Provisioning<br/><b>(Cloud Drivers)</b>"]
    Prov --> Conf["2. Configuration<br/><b>(Ansible Ground + User)</b>"]
    Conf --> Audit[("3. Audit Engine<br/><b>(Software & History)</b>")]

items.title: Step-by-Step Execution Pipeline
items.text: Stage Responsible Component Exactly What Executes Engineering Guarantee 1. Trigger Web UI Form / REST API / Schedulers (Celery Beat) Self-service web form submission, direct REST API call, or recurring scheduled job. Asynchronous, non-blocking ingestion with immediate HTTP response. 2. Authorization RBAC Engine & PostgreSQL Strict validation of requester permissions, team quotas, and immutable logging of the operation request. Zero anonymous or untracked operational requests. 3. Provisioning Multi-Cloud Driver Layer Downstream call to target provider (AWS, OpenStack, OpenShift, or Bare-Metal) to create the compute instance and assign IP/DNS. Consistent abstraction without vendor lock-in to proprietary APIs. 4. Ground Ops Ansible Core (Banking Baseline) Mandatory pre-user baseline: CIS operating system hardening, corporate TLS certificates, firewall policies, and monitoring agent deployment. 100% compliance guarantee: if Ground validation fails, provisioning is aborted immediately. 5. User Ops Ansible Runner (User Workload) Dynamic runtime variable injection and execution of user-defined playbooks (middleware, databases, microservices). Strict isolation between corporate infrastructure baseline and app logic. 6. Audit Audit Engine (PostgreSQL + MongoDB) Collection of final forensic telemetry: exact versions of all installed packages on the node, open ports, and execution event logs. Instant forensic compliance reports for internal auditors and regulators.

items.title: A. Hybrid Persistence: Relational Integrity vs. Document Flexibility
items.text: A single database engine could not simultaneously satisfy strict banking compliance and multi-cloud inventory scale: - PostgreSQL handles relational models requiring strict ACID transactions: RBAC permissions, product catalogs, state machines, and the immutable audit log. - MongoDB stores polymorphic documents detailing multi-cloud assets across tens of thousands of machines (where AWS instances, OpenStack VMs, and bare-metal nodes have completely disparate attribute trees), indexing the complete software tree for high-volume cross-estate querying. - Redis provides hot caching for frequent queries and serves as the high-throughput task queue broker for Celery workers.

items.title: B. Separation of Concerns: Two-Layer Ansible Pipeline
items.text: To eliminate configuration drift without bottlenecking development autonomy, automation is divided into two sequential layers: - Ground Layer (Corporate Guarantee): CIS operating system hardening, firewall rules, corporate TLS certificates, and monitoring agents. No compute instance progresses to user workload provisioning without a successful Ground check. - User Operation Layer (Application Autonomy): Isolated runtime variable injection to deploy application middleware, databases, and service configurations.

items.title: C. End-to-End Auditability & Lifecycle Traceability
items.text: Orion avoids delegating audit compliance to ephemeral pipeline logs. It maintains an immutable lifecycle ledger for each node: who authorized it, what configuration changes occurred over time, exact package and library versions installed, and full incident history. This establishes Orion as the technical foundation for complying with DORA (Regulation EU 2022/2554) ICT risk management and asset inventory mandates.

items.title: 5. Architectural Trade-Offs
items.text: Decision Alternative Considered Trade-Off Rationale Two-layer Ansible pipeline (Ground + User) Monolithic user-managed playbook Guarantees 100% compliance with corporate security, hardening, and monitoring standards without relying on individual team discipline. Centralized audit engine in Orion Traceability delegated to ephemeral pipeline logs Enables immediate responses to regulatory audits with complete forensic histories for every machine and its installed packages. Hybrid PostgreSQL + MongoDB Single relational DB with JSONB Retains strict relational integrity for RBAC and audit logs while providing high-performance indexing across heterogeneous cloud metadata and package inventories. In-house Python driver abstraction Separate cloud-specific tooling stacks Unifies permissions, operation catalogs, and governance in a vendor-neutral control plane.

items.title: 6. Operational & Business Impact
items.text:
• Cost efficiency & technology sovereignty: Consolidating an in-house control plane and HA dispatcher with native layered Ansible execution eliminated the need for commercial node-licensed automation suites (such as Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform), generating an estimated cumulative cost avoidance exceeding €6M in enterprise licensing fees for the organization.
  • Auditability & complete traceability (DORA Compliance): Reduced audit preparation from weeks of manual data compilation to instant queries covering any machine: who authorized it, what is installed, and its full historical event log — natively fulfilling ICT asset tracking requirements under DORA and European Central Bank inspections.
  • Enforced security & observability baseline (Ground): 100% of the 30,000+ managed machines run verified corporate security policies and monitoring agents from the moment of provisioning.
  • Self-service at banking scale: Over 500 engineers govern infrastructure autonomously, executing 40,000+ daily operations via web forms, REST APIs, and scheduled automations.
  • International adoption: Successfully deployed across multiple international banking divisions (Spain, Mexico, and Turkey).

items.title: WrenchBuddy: AI Vehicle Lifecycle & pgvector RAG Platform
items.text:
Dimension Details Role Creator & Maintainer (Open Source) Repositories oredondo/WrenchBuddy (Backend) · oredondo/WrenchBuddy-frontend (TypeScript) (Apache 2.0 License) Domain Full-stack backend architecture, asynchronous task queues, Vision OCR & pgvector RAG Stack Python 3.12, Django 6.0, Django REST Framework, PostgreSQL (pgvector), Celery 5.4, Redis, AWS S3 / MinIO (boto3), LangChain, ReportLab, Docker, TypeScript

Overview

While my enterprise work on Orion at BBVA is proprietary, WrenchBuddy is a public, production-structured Django + DRF + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL platform on GitHub. It combines relational domain modeling with 768-dimensional pgvector embeddings over technical workshop manuals, asynchronous Vision/OCR invoice parsing, S3-compatible media storage, and a context-injected conversational maintenance assistant for motorcycles and cars.

items.title: A. Unified Relational + Vector Storage (PostgreSQL + pgvector)
items.text:
Instead of introducing a separate external vector database that can drift out of sync with relational records, WrenchBuddy uses PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension:

  • Uploaded workshop manuals and technical specification sheets (PDF / images) are extracted asynchronously, split into semantic chunks, embedded into 768-dimensional vectors, and stored alongside the vehicle foreign keys in PostgreSQL.
  • Queries combine strict relational filtering (exact vehicle ID, ownership permissions) with cosine similarity search in a single database tier.

items.title: B. Asynchronous Vision/OCR Invoice Parsing & Smart Catalogs (Celery + Redis)
items.text:
Heavy I/O and LLM calls never block HTTP request threads:

  • Invoice & receipt extraction: When a user uploads a photo or PDF of a workshop invoice, a Celery task invokes vision and text models to automatically extract performed labor, replaced parts, odometer readings, and itemized costs into structured maintenance records.
  • Smart task catalog synthesis: Background jobs synthesize periodic maintenance schedules tailored to exact vehicle make, model, year, displacement, and riding conditions.

items.title: C. Grounded Vehicle-Contextual RAG Assistant (ai_assistant/)
items.text:
When a user asks a natural-language question about service intervals, torque specs, or historical repairs, the LangChain pipeline injects:

  1. The vehicle's real specifications and current odometer state.
  2. Computed maintenance schedules and historical invoice records.
  3. Top-K retrieved technical manual chunks from pgvector — responding in the user's configured language (English or Spanish).

items.title: D. Portable Cloud-Native Storage & PDF Dossier Export
items.text:
• S3 / MinIO abstraction: Media attachments (manuals, invoices, garage galleries) use django-storages and boto3, switching seamlessly between local storage, self-hosted MinIO, and AWS S3 via environment configuration.
  • ReportLab PDF export: Generates downloadable full-history vehicle condition and maintenance dossiers for resale or workshop handoff.
